issues.legal_issue: A plaint cannot be rejected as barred by res judicata at the threshold when the plaint alleges fraud and collusion and deciding the bar requires inquiry beyond the plaint.
material_facts: A society that was not a party to an earlier suit for specific performance claimed ownership of the disputed land under gift deeds.
The society’s execution objections and its application to set aside the earlier decree were unsuccessful.
The society later filed a declaratory suit alleging that the earlier decree and related transactions were fraudulent and collusive.
The defendants sought rejection of the plaint under Order VII Rule 11(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure on the ground of res judicata.

The trial court relied on the written statement as well as the plaint to reject the plaint; the High Court restored that rejection, although the Supreme Court found that the fraud and collusion allegations and the distinct grounds raised in the suit required a trial.
issues.conclusion: The appeal was allowed, the High Court’s order was set aside, and the order restoring the suit was reinstated. On the plaint alone, the suit could not be held barred by res judicata; the framed issues required trial.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order VII Rule 11(d) of the Code of Civil Procedure, whether a suit is barred by law must be determined from the plaint alone, without adding to or subtracting from its averments or considering evidence or the written statement. Res judicata may involve mixed questions of fact and law and must be established on the basis of the prior pleadings, issues, and judgment; where that requires factual inquiry, it cannot be determined at the plaint-rejection stage. The Court relied on V. Rajeshwari v. T.C. Saravanabava, Kamala v. K.T. Eshwara SA, and Balasaria Construction (P) Ltd. v. Hanuman Seva Trust.

predicates.order_7_rule_11_d_application: A defendant applied to have the plaint rejected on the ground that the suit was barred by law.
predicates.plaint_alleges_fraud_or_collusion: The plaint alleges that the earlier judgment or proceeding was brought about by fraud or collusion.
predicates.res_judicata_requires_factual_inquiry: Deciding whether the earlier proceeding bars the suit requires inquiry into facts or matters beyond the plaint.

issues.definition: When a defendant seeks rejection of a plaint on a res judicata ground, the plaint is not rejected at the threshold if it alleges fraud or collusion and deciding the bar requires factual inquiry.

issues.legal_issue: An appellate court should not interfere with concurrent refusals to set aside a judgment when the lower courts have considered the facts and no merit in the challenge is shown.
material_facts: An application under Order IX Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure sought to set aside a judgment in an earlier civil suit.
The trial court declined to entertain the application, and the appellate court affirmed that decision after analysing the facts.
The High Court declined to interfere in revision.
The Supreme Court found no merit in the appeal challenging the High Court’s refusal to interfere.
issues.conclusion: The appeal was dismissed, with no order as to costs.
issues.legal_principle: The Court stated that the trial court and appellate court had analysed the facts in detail and that there was no merit in the appeal; it did not articulate a broader legal test. The proceeding concerned an application under Order IX Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure to set aside a judgment.

predicates.appeal_challenges_refusal_to_set_aside_j: The appeal challenges a refusal to grant an application seeking to set aside a judgment.
predicates.lower_courts_examined_facts: The trial and appellate courts considered the facts in detail before refusing the application.
predicates.appeal_shows_no_merit: The Supreme Court finds no merit in the challenge to the lower courts’ decisions.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges refusal of an application to set aside a judgment, the lower courts examined the facts, and the challenge has no merit, the appeal is dismissed.
